claim: Anthropic's Research system (lead Claude Opus 4 + Sonnet 4 subagents, 90.2% over single-agent) requires each subagent brief to specify an objective, an output format, tool/source guidance and task boundaries.
quote: Each subagent needs an objective, an output format, guidance on the tools and sources to use, and clear task boundaries. Without detailed task descriptions, agents duplicate work, leave gaps, or fail to find necessary information.
why: Primary production precedent: the hand-off contract is defined by the lead, and output format is a required part of the brief.

claim: Anthropic recommends subagents write outputs to a filesystem/artifact store and return lightweight references to the lead, to avoid a 'game of telephone' and token overhead.
quote: Subagents call tools to store their work in external systems, then pass lightweight references back to the coordinator. This prevents information loss during multi-stage processing and reduces token overhead from copying large outputs through conversation history.
why: Supports hunters writing cards to files (cards-Qn.jsonl) and handing back a path, not pasting content.

claim: In Anthropic's Research system citations are attached after synthesis by a separate CitationAgent that locates specific citation positions in the source documents.
quote: passes all findings to a CitationAgent, which processes the documents and research report to identify specific locations for citations. This ensures all claims are properly attributed to their sources.
why: Shows an alternative design: provenance resolved late by a dedicated agent rather than carried in each hunter card; relevant to citation handling.

claim: Anthropic's open-source research_subagent prompt tells subagents to flag speculation and problematic sources and to pass unresolved conflicting information to the lead rather than resolve it.
quote: If unable to reconcile facts, include the conflicting information in your final task report for the lead researcher to resolve.
why: Directly supports 'do not over-filter, hand doubtful evidence up with flags' - the hunter reports, the lead adjudicates.

claim: Anthropic's context-engineering post (2025-09-29) says subagents may use tens of thousands of tokens but return a condensed summary of often 1,000-2,000 tokens.
quote: Each subagent might explore extensively, using tens of thousands of tokens or more, but returns only a condensed, distilled summary of its work (often 1,000-2,000 tokens).
why: Gives a concrete size budget for hunter hand-offs (8-14 cards fits ~1-2k tokens).

claim: Claude Agent SDK docs: a subagent's only channel back is its final message, returned verbatim as the Agent tool result; intermediate tool calls stay inside the subagent.
quote: The parent receives the subagent's final message verbatim as the Agent tool result, but may summarize it in its own response.
why: Platform constraint for research-stack: anything the gatherer needs (paths, card counts, gaps) must be in the final message or in files it references.

claim: LangChain open_deep_research returns two artifacts per researcher: 'compressed_research' (LLM-cleaned findings with numbered citations) and 'raw_notes' (concatenated raw tool and AI message content).
why: Strong open-source precedent for handing both a compressed summary and raw notes, matching the brief's cards + raw-Qn.md design.

claim: open_deep_research's compress_research prompt forbids summarizing, requires verbatim preservation and a fixed 3-part format (queries/tool calls, findings, all sources numbered 1,2,3 without gaps).
quote: It's really important not to lose any sources. A later LLM will be used to merge this report with others, so having all of the sources is critical.
why: Shows the compression step is designed as near-lossless cleanup with mandatory query log and source list, not a summary.

claim: OpenAI deep research API output exposes intermediate web_search_call items (search/open_page/find_in_page) plus a message whose url_citation annotations carry url, title, start_index and end_index.
quote: It will contain a listing of web search calls, code interpreter calls, and remote MCP calls made to get to the answer.
why: Vendor schema for provenance: span-level citations plus a log of queries actually run (analogue of the hunter's raw notes).

claim: STORM (NAACL 2024) keeps a reference pool R from simulated Q&A conversations and, at writing time, retrieves from R per section via Sentence-BERT similarity because R does not fit in context.
quote: Since it is usually impossible to fit the entire R within the context window of the LLM, we use the section title and headings of its all-level subsections to retrieve relevant documents from R based on semantic similarity
why: Alternate pattern: hunters deposit raw references into a pool, curator retrieves per section; editors also flagged 'over-association of unrelated facts'.

claim: GPT Researcher compresses scraped pages by chunking (1000 chars, 100 overlap) and filtering chunks with an embedding similarity threshold defaulting to 0.35, tracking visited_urls for sources.
why: Contrast case: non-LLM, query-similarity compression with no hunter reasoning recorded; shows the cheap end of the design space.

claim: AgentIR (Chen et al., Waterloo/CMU) finds embedding the agent's reasoning trace with its query lifts BrowseComp-Plus accuracy to 68% vs 52% for a 2x larger query-only embedder and 37% for BM25.
quote: Deep Research agents generate explicit natural language reasoning before each search, revealing rich intent and context that existing retrievers entirely ignore.
why: Evidence that the hunter's 'why fetched' reasoning is useful signal for downstream relevance judgment; note it is retrieval-side, not curator-side (preprint, not clearly peer-reviewed).

claim: DeepTRACE (2025-09) audit finds deep-research agents' citation accuracy ranges 40-80% and many statements are unsupported by their own listed sources.
quote: they remain highly one-sided on debate queries and still exhibit large fractions of unsupported statements, with citation accuracy ranging from 40–80% across systems.
why: Motivates mandatory verbatim quote + URL per card so the gatherer can verify support instead of trusting citations.

claim: 'Cited but Not Verified' benchmarks 14 LLMs: links valid >94% and relevant >80%, but Fact Check only 39-77%, and Fact Check drops ~42% as tool calls scale from 2 to 150.
quote: Fact Check accuracy drops approximately 42% on average across two frontier models as tool calls scale from 2 to 150, demonstrating that more retrieval does not produce more accurate citations.
why: Supports small per-hunter budgets and quote-level provenance; relevant to hunter tool-call budget (15-20). Recent preprint; numbers unverified elsewhere.
